charts.title: Search and screening funnel
charts.subtitle: Read each block top to bottom: every bar is one step of the pipeline, the number is what was left after it, and the grey note says what that step removed.

charts.title: Competitor crowding by category
charts.subtitle: Each bar counts the verified products in one category; longer bars mean a more crowded market. Colours split each category by how products charge.

charts.title: Evidence profile
charts.subtitle: Four views of the same quotes: what people said, how strong the evidence is (S0 opinion up to S4 money spent), what kind of page it came from, and which websites supplied it.

charts.title: Price ladder
charts.subtitle: Each dot is one product's cheapest paid plan per month (USD); the dark tick and the number on the right are the category median. Cheapest categories at the top. The scale is logarithmic, so equal distances mean equal price ratios.

charts.title: Run effort and amendments
charts.subtitle: Left: subagents assigned per pipeline phase, in the order they ran. Right: the running total over the run, with each protocol amendment marked by its number (listed below).

charts.title: Options by kind and evidence
charts.subtitle: Each bar is one lens (kind of opportunity); its segments show how far the evidence got: promising, thin, not tested yet, contradicted, or excluded by red flags, gates or the protocol. 8 were tested with evidence.

charts.title: Opportunity map
charts.subtitle: Each dot is one option. Right = stronger signals in the market map (traction, prices, platforms, catalysts); up = more verified evidence (distinct authors, weighted by evidence strength). The best options sit top right; the top 10 by rank are labelled.

charts.title: Proven but poorly rated products
charts.subtitle: Each dot is one marketplace product. Right = more installs or ratings than others in its store (percentile); down = lower average rating. Products right of the line are proven; ringed ones are also in the bottom third of their store's ratings, the raw material of 'proven product + one fix' options.

charts.title: Platform coverage
charts.subtitle: Rows are categories, columns are platforms; each cell counts the mapped products. Empty cells next to full ones are candidate ports; outlined cells are the ones the scan turned into options.
